interface_debt.why: cfe.h pulls in the full cFE service surface, so all 16 consumer repositories become coupled to every service header. When cFE adds, removes, or changes any of these headers, every consumer must be recompiled and may need include or API changes even if it uses only one service.
interface_debt.better: Require applications to include only the specific cFE service headers they need and keep cfe.h, if retained, as a thin legacy convenience header rather than the primary dependency.
interface_debt.title: cFE:modules/core_api/fsw/inc/cfe.h: cfe.h — one header carries unrelated responsibilities

interface_debt.quote: include "osapi.h" /* Define OS API function prototypes
interface_debt.why: The cFE umbrella makes every consumer transitively depend on the OSAL public interface. An OSAL API change, include-path change, or platform-specific OSAL variant forces all 16 repositories to rebuild or adapt even when cFE's own API is unchanged.
interface_debt.better: Keep OSAL out of the cFE service headers; expose cFE types and APIs only, and let applications include osapi.h directly when they need OS services.
interface_debt.title: cFE:modules/core_api/fsw/inc/cfe.h: osapi.h — a declaration whose meaning or signature is likely to change

interface_debt.quote: include "cfe_psp.h" /* Define Platform Support Package API
interface_debt.why: Including the Platform Support Package API in the general cFE header forces all consumers to depend on PSP, which is often platform- or mission-specific. PSP changes or a different PSP implementation can break or require coordinated changes across all 16 repositories.
interface_debt.better: Limit PSP includes to components that directly use PSP services and keep the core cFE application contract independent of platform-specific support APIs.
interface_debt.title: cFE:modules/core_api/fsw/inc/cfe.h: cfe_psp.h — a declaration whose meaning or signature is likely to change

interface_debt.why: Every user that converts a status to text must size its buffer to 11; if cFE later uses a longer or differently formatted status string, all 16 repositories must change buffer sizes and code that assumes the old width may truncate or overflow.
interface_debt.better: Do not publish a fixed string length; provide a conversion API that takes a caller buffer and its size or returns the required length, and keep the internal format size private.
interface_debt.title: cFE:modules/core_api/fsw/inc/cfe_error.h: CFE_STATUS_STRING_LENGTH — a macro hard-codes a size, an offset or a layout

interface_debt.why: The public type is a fixed 11-byte array, so user declarations and function calls depend on that exact layout; changing the length changes the type and breaks every user that declares or passes CFE_StatusString_t.
interface_debt.better: Use char * plus size_t in the public string API, or expose a length-query function instead of a fixed-size array type.
interface_debt.title: cFE:modules/core_api/fsw/inc/cfe_error.h: CFE_StatusString_t — users reach into the layout of a type (public struct or union members)

interface_debt.why: It exposes the bit position of the service field in the 32-bit status; users may mask or shift status values to identify the service. If cFE widens, moves, or repurposes that field, raw bit tests in user code break or silently misclassify codes.
interface_debt.better: Keep the status bit layout internal and expose accessors such as CFE_StatusGetService() or CFE_StatusIsService(); avoid publishing raw bit masks as public contract.
interface_debt.title: cFE:modules/core_api/fsw/inc/cfe_error.h: CFE_SERVICE_BITMASK — a macro hard-codes a size, an offset or a layout

interface_debt.why: It freezes the severity field at the top two bits; users may use it to distinguish success, informational, and error statuses. Adding a new severity, changing the encoding, or moving the field forces every user that performs raw bit tests to change.
interface_debt.better: Provide severity predicates or a CFE_StatusGetSeverity() function and keep raw severity masks private.
interface_debt.title: cFE:modules/core_api/fsw/inc/cfe_error.h: CFE_SEVERITY_BITMASK — a macro hard-codes a size, an offset or a layout

interface_debt.why: The API is tied to the fixed CFE_StatusString_t buffer and returns the caller's pointer; any change to the string length, format, or ownership model requires changing this prototype and every user call site.
interface_debt.better: Use a size-aware API such as int CFE_ES_StatusToString(char *buf, size_t buf_len, CFE_Status_t status) or return a const char * with no caller buffer.
interface_debt.title: cFE:modules/core_api/fsw/inc/cfe_error.h: CFE_ES_StatusToString — a declaration whose meaning or signature is likely to change

interface_debt.why: The status type is a raw int32, so all users can store, compare, and pass arbitrary 32-bit values and rely on the signed integer representation; if cFE later changes the width, sign, or makes the type opaque for type safety, every user must change.
interface_debt.better: Use an opaque or enum-like status type with accessor functions, or at least keep the underlying representation internal and expose only stable conversion helpers.
interface_debt.title: cFE:modules/core_api/fsw/inc/cfe_error.h: CFE_Status_t — a type fixes its representation (union for aliasing, fixed-size array, bitfield)

interface_debt.quote: CFE_ES_DTEST(m[(s) / 32], (s) % 32)) /* Test a bit within an array of 32-bit integers.
interface_debt.why: Users test bits in a long mask by directly indexing a 32-bit word array. If cFE later changes the mask word size, alignment, or resource count, this macro either computes the wrong word or stops compiling, forcing all user call sites to change together with cFE.
interface_debt.better: Expose an opaque bitset type and provide CFE_ES_TestLongMask() or a macro that uses a documented word-size constant, not a hard-coded 32.
interface_debt.title: cFE:modules/core_api/fsw/inc/cfe_es.h: CFE_ES_TEST_LONG_MASK — a macro hard-codes a size, an offset or a layout

interface_debt.quote: define CFE_ES_DBIT(x) (1L << (x)) /* Places a one at bit positions 0 thru 31
interface_debt.why: The macro freezes bit positions 0 through 31 and uses long as the mask width. If cFE supports more than 31 bits or changes the expected mask width, user code using this macro becomes undefined behavior or silently wrong, requiring coordinated changes in every user repository.
interface_debt.better: Use a fixed-width type such as uint32_t for bit masks and provide a typed helper or macro that documents the supported bit range.
interface_debt.title: cFE:modules/core_api/fsw/inc/cfe_es.h: CFE_ES_DBIT — a macro hard-codes a size, an offset or a layout
